name: Museo Reina Sofía
funding: State museum. Corporate patrons: Inditex, Fundación la Caixa, Fundación Mapfre, Fundación Mutua Madrileña. Partners include Estrella Damm, HP, Iberia, Madrid city and region.
watch: National museum of modern art in Madrid.
why_flagged: la Caixa's holding Criteria is the largest shareholder of gas utility Naturgy, 23% of its 2025 dividends. No Repsol, Endesa or Iberdrola listed.
records_note: It posts annual activity reports 2002 to 2025, yearly accounts, a named sponsors page and the Real Patronato members.

name: Museo Soumaya
funding: Owned and paid for by Fundación Carlos Slim; entry is free at both sites.
watch: Name to know: Carlos Slim. Mexico's regulator ruled América Móvil's units dominant in 2014. His CICSA agreed to repair Metro Line 12 after 26 deaths.
why_flagged: Name to know: Carlos Slim. Mexico's regulator ruled América Móvil's units dominant in 2014. His CICSA agreed to repair Metro Line 12 after 26 deaths.
records_note: The museum and its owner publish no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; Fundación Carlos Slim owns and pays for it.

name: Museo Tamayo
records_note: No annual reports or accounts found; the foundation page names its board and international council, while corporate sponsors appear as undated logos.

name: Museu de Arte Moderna de São Paulo
watch: Grupo Ultra (Ipiranga fuel distribution) is a master sponsor.
why_flagged: Grupo Ultra (Ipiranga fuel distribution) is a master sponsor.
records_note: MAM São Paulo posts annual reports for 2018 to 2025, audited statements for the same years, sponsor logos by tier undated, and its boards.

name: Museu de Arte Moderna do Rio de Janeiro
records_note: MAM Rio posts activity reports for 2020 and 2021 only, no accounts, sponsor logos by tier without a date, and its board and fiscal council.

name: Museu do Amanhã
funding: Run by IDG with the City of Rio and Fundação Roberto Marinho. Itaú is strategic sponsor; Shell, Instituto Cultural Vale and Motiva are maintainers; IBM, TAG and Bloomberg also give.
watch: Shell and Instituto Cultural Vale are named maintainers. Vale's Brumadinho dam collapse killed 270 in 2019. Over 8 million visitors in its first decade.
why_flagged: Run by IDG with the City of Rio and Fundação Roberto Marinho. Itaú is strategic sponsor; Shell, Instituto Cultural Vale and Motiva are maintainers; IBM, TAG and Bloomberg also give.
records_note: Reports for 2020 to 2022 are in its archive, supporters are named undated, the IDG board is listed, and its accounts page failed to load.

name: Museum Folkwang
watch: RWE and E.ON as exhibition partners.
why_flagged: RWE and E.ON as exhibition partners.
records_note: Museum Folkwang names 11 sponsors and 29 donors undated and lists its Board of Trustees, but posts no annual report or accounts.

name: Museum MACAN
watch: Founder money partly from petroleum distribution.
why_flagged: Founder money partly from petroleum distribution.
records_note: Museum MACAN names its individual patrons undated but posts no annual report, accounts or board; its leadership page names only the foundation chair.

name: Museum of Art & Photography (MAP)
funding: Private museum of the Art & Photography Foundation. Founder Abhishek Poddar gave the collection and his family the land. Building donors include Kiran Mazumdar Shaw, Sunil Munjal, Citi and Tata.
watch: In 2016 artists held a sit-in and a 1,000-signature petition against a state deal giving its parent foundation the Venkatappa Art Gallery.
why_flagged: Private museum of the Art & Photography Foundation. Founder Abhishek Poddar gave the collection and his family the land. Building donors include Kiran Mazumdar Shaw, Sunil Munjal, Citi and Tata.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2020-21 to 2025-26 and audited statements from 2014-15, names its trustees, and shows founding patrons only as logos.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art Belgrade
funding: Funded by Serbia's Ministry of Culture; the museum publishes the ministry's financial plans for 2023 to 2026.
watch: On 30 January 2020 the government replaced acting director Slobodan Nakarada with Viktor Kiš despite a 2019 open call. Board chair resigned; CIMAM objected.
why_flagged: Funded by Serbia's Ministry of Culture; the museum publishes the ministry's financial plans for 2023 to 2026. No corporate sponsor list found.
records_note: A 2022 report, final accounts for 2020 and 2021, a recent balance sheet and financial plans are posted; no funder list or board is named.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo
funding: Tokyo Metropolitan Government museum; budget about ¥1B.
watch: Bloomberg is a current funder (Students Day, Oct 2026). Also a censorship row in Jul 2015, when MOT and Tokyo asked for an Aida family work to be removed and then withdrew the request.
why_flagged: Bloomberg is a current funder (Students Day, Oct 2026). Also a censorship row in Jul 2015, when MOT and Tokyo asked for an Aida family work to be removed and then withdrew the request.
records_note: MOT posts annual reports for fiscal 2008 to 2025; its operator foundation posts financial statements for 2015 to 2025 and names directors. No sponsor list.

name: Museum of Fine Arts Budapest / Hungarian National Gallery
funding: Hungarian state museum. 2026 main and featured sponsors: MVM Group (energy, sells gas), E.ON Energiamegoldások, OTP Bank, MBH Bank, Szerencsejáték Zrt. (state lottery), PPG Trilak, Veolia Energia.
watch: Szerencsejáték also runs Tippmix sports betting; as with Loto-Québec, a state lottery operator is a name to know, not a flag. In April 2026 director László Baán quit the National Cultural Fund committee, writing that many grants did not fit its aims. The minister disputed this.
why_flagged: Hungarian state museum. 2026 main and featured sponsors: MVM Group (energy, sells gas), E.ON Energiamegoldások, OTP Bank, MBH Bank, Szerencsejáték Zrt. (state lottery), PPG Trilak, Veolia Energia.
records_note: It posts yearly budget reports for 2014 to 2025 and budgets to 2026, names its 2026 sponsors, and lists management but no board.
